Onboarding simplification also compounds with whatever we do next, whereas the competitor-driven pull toward promotional_pricing carries the clearest downstream value risk: memory_73's readout is explicitly a four-week window on the standard SMB segment with the usual cadence, which is long enough to see acquisition and revenue lift but too short to see discount-cohort retention, margin erosion, or price-anchoring damage — exactly the failure mode that converts short-term revenue into unsustainable revenue against the long-term qualified-revenue objective. So I spend verification where it changes a decision: memory_73 to test whether its lift survives past the four-week horizon (if it does, and includes retention, pricing becomes a live contender against a real competitive threat), and memory_86 to confirm the onboarding effect is a genuine completion/time-to-value gain rather than a funnel-shortening artifact that merely moves drop-off downstream or admits lower-intent accounts. I am not verifying memory_31 (redundant with memory_86 and the older, weaker record), memory_57 (referral incentives address neither declining metric and presuppose an already-activated base), or memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist is a different segment from the SMB accounts under attack, and reallocating the single slot there abandons both declining metrics).
